ranked.headline: Graph and Gaussian-process models embed spatial priors in transcriptomics analysis
ranked.summary: Recent spatial transcriptomics methods encode neighborhood structure into graph, kernel, and attention models for domain, gene, and cell-type inference.

ranked.headline: Explicit statistical models now drive cell-state and outcome inference from omics data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications pair explicit deconvolution, conformal, and Bayesian models with single-cell and bulk omics for phenotypic inference.

ranked.headline: Learned models are generating and screening peptides and small molecules against targets
ranked.summary: Generative and predictive models now span structure-aware screening, peptide design, and target deconvolution across recent preprints and papers.

ranked.headline: Pretrained protein language models underpin residue-level binding site prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers pair protein language model embeddings with graph, hypergraph, and equivariant architectures for binding site prediction.

ranked.headline: Spatial transcriptomics methods link cell states to tissue geometry and morphology
ranked.summary: Spatial transcriptomics tools now infer cell size, senescent cell organization and spatial statistics directly from expression and position data.

ranked.headline: Simulation and scattering tools resolve membrane, condensate and protein physics
ranked.summary: Simulation and Bayesian scattering analysis now yield quantitative membrane, condensate, and protein-packing parameters from atomistic and experimental data.

ranked.headline: Retrieval and LLMs are attaching literature-derived functional context to genes
ranked.summary: Recent items pair literature-derived context with LLM annotation, enrichment, and omics integration, extending gene-level annotation toward prioritization.

ranked.headline: Prior-constrained inference of dependency structure from high-dimensional omics data
ranked.summary: Recent items couple prior knowledge, latent factors and trajectory context to network and score estimation across single-cell and multi-omics data.

ranked.headline: Deep learning models correct and filter sequencing-derived variant and splice calls
ranked.summary: Long-read and transcriptome error correction is increasingly handled by sequence-level deep learning and genomic language models.

ranked.headline: Learned representations drive peptide structure prediction and functional annotation
ranked.summary: Structure predictors now extend to non-natural peptide chemistry, with benchmarks testing their accuracy on short peptides.

ranked.headline: Pretrained protein language models are adapted, not retrained, for downstream tasks
ranked.summary: Recent papers adapt protein language model features via layer-selective tuning and contrastive pretraining across antibody and pathogenicity tasks.

ranked.headline: Sequence-based inference of rare, structural and complex variants at population scale
ranked.summary: Pangenome references, long-read data and 1000 Genomes-scale cohorts now allow genotyping of rare, novel and structurally complex variants.

ranked.headline: Fusing multimodal representations for drug, protein and cell-response prediction
ranked.summary: Recent methods pair sequence, 3D structure, knowledge-graph and language-model embeddings, with fusion benefits resting on task-specific benchmarks.

ranked.headline: Evaluating structure predictors and generators for TCR and antibody antigen binding
ranked.summary: Strict out-of-distribution splits and negative-data quality are replacing architecture as the basis for judging binding prediction tools.

ranked.headline: Comparative genomes reveal convergent adaptation and lineage-specific genome organization
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers pair long-read reference genomes with multi-lineage comparisons of convergent adaptation and sex-linked genome structure.

ranked.headline: Computational methods refine DMR calling, TF binding, and regulatory interpretation
ranked.summary: Recent papers pair replicate-aware methylation analysis with sequence-based models of regulatory function and TF binding.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking and computational design of CRISPR perturbation screens and Cas nucleases
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a bioinformatics paper benchmark CRISPR knockout versus interference and model Cas9 efficiency and kinetic fidelity.

ranked.headline: Tools infer microbial relations, taxonomy, and resistance gene co-occurrence
ranked.summary: Recent tools target false taxonomic identifications, molecular interspecies interactions, and resistance gene co-occurrence in microbial communities.

ranked.headline: Computational tools for protein modification, localization and proteomic translation
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and resource updates test how accurately computational tools predict protein features across platforms and datasets.

ranked.headline: Compressed indexes and graph structures for querying pangenome sequence directly
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications report memory-light mapping, coordinate queries and compressed move-structure indexes for pangenome data.

ranked.headline: Geometric descriptors and distance priors quantify protein and RNA structural features
ranked.summary: Structure predictors are being extended with distance priors and per-residue quality measures that go beyond pLDDT on whole proteomes.

ranked.headline: Fitting mechanistic PDE and ODE models to snapshot, spatial, and single-molecule data
ranked.summary: Static snapshots, sparse recordings, and imaging data now constrain biophysical models, with identifiability limits becoming an explicit question.

ranked.headline: Learned models move from static protein structures toward dynamic ensembles
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply diffusion, Bayesian and deep learning models to protein dynamics, ensembles and cryo-EM heterogeneity.

ranked.headline: Read-level inference replaces aggregated calls for copy number and methylation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers estimate copy number, methylation, and antigen specificity directly from raw reads rather than finalized calls.

ranked.headline: Unbalanced optimal transport models population mass change in single-cell dynamics
ranked.summary: Unpaired and cross-sectional profiles are now modeled with unbalanced transport, which lets population mass change alongside state shifts.

ranked.headline: Response models for drugs and dose schedules are tested against reference data
ranked.summary: Recent ML, RL, and pharmacogenomic papers and preprints test drug response and dosing models against measured reference data.

ranked.headline: Interactive web and R tools for exploring and sharing omics analysis results
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers describe packaged, reproducible tools making proteomics, transcriptomics, and DamID outputs explorable and shareable.

ranked.headline: Gene flow and asymmetric dependence complicate phylogenetic inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers introduce methods that quantify or detect gene flow and asymmetric dependence affecting phylogenetic conclusions.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking and diagnostics that check the outputs of computational biology tools
ranked.summary: Reliability of upstream computational stages now depends on explicit, benchmarked checks of tool outputs rather than on any single algorithm.

ranked.headline: Strong benchmark scores in pLM and ADMET work may reflect shortcuts and leakage
ranked.summary: Attribution controls and a leaderboard audit show that reported benchmark gains may not reflect the intended biological task.

ranked.headline: Network topology as the inferential object in gene regulation and rare-variant testing
ranked.summary: Recent work embeds gene, protein, and hypergraph topology directly into inference for regulatory networks, rare variants, and personalized cancer therapy.

ranked.headline: Read-level evidence defines RNA boundaries and cleavage sites
ranked.summary: Strand-specific and dRNA-seq reads now support explicit boundary calls for bacterial sRNAs and mitochondrial RNA cleavage sites.

ranked.headline: Compressed k-mer indexes and GPU phylogenetics push scalable sequence analysis
ranked.summary: Petabyte-scale k-mer indexes and phylogenetic datasets with millions of entries make memory-efficient representations a pressing requirement.

ranked.headline: Context-resolved networks recover regulators and circuits that global inference misses
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a journal article test context-specific network and embedding methods on regulators, knowledge graphs, and single-cell models.

ranked.headline: Open-source software for processing and analyzing imaging and spatial omics data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and journal articles release Python and Rust tools for routine processing of neuroimaging, microscopy, and spatial omics data.

ranked.headline: Causal, kernel, and multi-trait methods extend genetic association testing
ranked.summary: Recent methods integrate Hi-C 3D structure, multi-tissue instruments, and multi-outcome designs into genetic association analysis.

ranked.headline: Multimodal computational frameworks link omics, imaging and simulation in immune biology
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs single-cell, spatial and receptor-sequence data with learned fusion, simulation or AI image analysis to resolve immune cell states.

ranked.headline: Quantitative models probe kinetics, memory capacity and microbial dynamics
ranked.summary: Preprints apply information theory, stochastic modelling and machine learning to estimate kinetic parameters and information capacity in biological systems.

ranked.headline: Multi-agent LLM frameworks automate bioinformatics analysis and experiment execution
ranked.summary: Between July 3 and 8, 2026, LLM multi-agent systems were reported for bioinformatics, trajectory inference, and pharmacometric modeling.

ranked.headline: Learned models of tandem MS spectra are reshaping metabolite annotation
ranked.summary: Setup-independent transformer models and AI platforms are addressing annotation and processing bottlenecks in untargeted LC-MS metabolomics.
